GMW.Settings.CustomModelHint: Used for “auto” when this is the only key set. After “Check” you can pick from the list.
GMW.Settings.AdvancedIntro: Which model to use for each task. “Auto” is fine almost always. The model list appears after you “Check” a key.
GMW.Settings.RoleLoreHint: Questions about the adventure, NPCs, session recaps. The strongest model.
GMW.Settings.RoleTacticsHint: A monster's combat turn with the map in mind.
GMW.Settings.RoleFastHint: “Fast” mode, NPC lines. A cheap, fast model.
GMW.Settings.ServerUrlHint: No need to change it if the server runs on this same computer.
GMW.Settings.OriginsHint: Only if Foundry is opened from another computer. Comma-separated, with https://. Applies after a server restart.
GMW.Settings.CampaignIntro: The model gets this information about your game with every question. Fill it in once and the answers will be about your world, not something generic.
GMW.Settings.CampNameHint: What to call the campaign in answers and the diary.
GMW.Settings.CampDescPlaceholder: A short blurb about your campaign. 2–5 sentences: where and when it takes place, who your adventuring party is and what they're fighting for.
GMW.Settings.CampDescHint: Goes into every request to the model — without it, the model answers “about the book in general”, not about your game.
GMW.Settings.CampTonePlaceholder: Grim in the world, lively at the table; NPCs talk like real people; keep it short.
GMW.Settings.CampToneHint: How the model should speak to the GM and as NPCs.
GMW.Settings.CampRulesPlaceholder: What overrides the system's general rules; name spellings; what not to use.
GMW.Settings.CampRulesHint: The model ranks these above the rulebooks.
GMW.Settings.CampLangHint: “Same as Foundry” — the GM's interface language.
GMW.Settings.LengthNormal: normal — the gist plus some detail
GMW.Settings.CampLengthHint: For adventure questions and rules discussions. “Recap” and “Prep” are always detailed.
GMW.Settings.CampLinesOnly: NPC lines — just the lines, no explanations or advice
GMW.Settings.CampNoImprov: Don't improvise when the materials have no answer (just say there isn't one)
GMW.Settings.CampPlayerNames: Mention the player next to the character: “Character name (Player name)”
GMW.Settings.SourcesIntro: For each journal folder, say what it is: GM notes, diary, adventure book, world description, rules — or “exclude”. When sources contradict each other, GM notes rank highest, then the diary, the book, the world, the rules. “Auto” — the module decides by folder name (the automatic choice is shown to the right after the arrow). Nested folders inherit the parent's type. The knowledge base rebuilds itself after saving.
GMW.Settings.KindGmHint: cheat sheets, NPC database, character backstories — highest priority when sources disagree
GMW.Settings.KindAdventureHint: the text of the original adventure
GMW.Settings.KindExcludeHint: not added to the knowledge base
GMW.Settings.PacksIntro: (compendiums) — tick the ones the advisor should use to answer rules questions.
GMW.Settings.NoPacks: This world has no journal compendiums.
GMW.Settings.BibleIntro: The essentials of the campaign on one page — the party, key NPCs, table rules, where the party is now. The model gets it with every question, so it answers much better about your game specifically. Lives in the “{name}” journal.
GMW.Settings.BibleExistsNote: You can add to the “Permanent” page right in the journal — the module never changes it; “Current State” refreshes itself after every “Recap”.
GMW.Settings.BibleMissingNote: It will be built from character sheets, their backstories, session recaps and the knowledge base (1–3 minutes).
GMW.Settings.BibleFolderHint: Backstories, biographies — what the players wrote about their heroes. Needed only to build the first bible.
GMW.Settings.BibleRebuildHint: On rebuild, the old version stays in the journal, marked with the date.
GMW.Settings.VoiceIntro: The Craig bot records voice in Discord. After the game, download the recording from the bot as an archive into the chosen folder (or set up Craig's cloud upload — a paid bot feature). Point to the folder and the recording will be picked up for “Recap”. Best download format: multitrack FLAC; AAC/MP3 work too.
GMW.Settings.CraigFolderHint: Full path, as in Explorer. Empty — voice isn't used.
GMW.Settings.CraigAuto: Transcribe new recordings as soon as they appear in the folder (otherwise — when writing a “Recap”)
GMW.Settings.SpeechLangHint: The language spoken at the table — makes recognition more accurate.
GMW.Settings.SpeakersIntro: Discord nicknames appear here on their own after the first transcription. On the right, write how to label the person in the diary — usually name and character: “Player name (Character name)”.
GMW.Settings.SpeakersEmpty: Empty for now: participants' names will appear here after the first Craig transcription.
GMW.Settings.IgnoreVoiceHint: Part of the nickname, comma-separated. For example, “kenku” keeps the “Kenku#1234” track out of the transcript.
GMW.Settings.IgnoreChatHint: If you don't want messages from some module or author sent to the model, enter the author name as shown in Foundry chat. Several — comma-separated.
GMW.Settings.Cleanup: Move old session records to the archive (the Foundry diary is untouched)
GMW.Settings.KeepDaysHint: The most recent session is never archived.

GMW.Setup.Title: GM Whispers — first run
GMW.Setup.WelcomeWhat: It's a GM assistant. It reads your world's journals and answers questions about the adventure with links to the pages, suggests a monster's move in the current fight, writes session recaps into the diary and prepares a briefing before the game. The players see none of it ;)
GMW.Setup.WelcomeParts: A Foundry module and a small program, {core}, on the GM's computer — it stores the knowledge base and talks to the AI model. The model needs a key from one of the services: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter or a compatible one.
GMW.Setup.WelcomeCost: The key spends tokens, and tokens cost money — but not much, especially if you don't ask everything under the sun for fun. You pay only the AI service through your own key, usually under a dollar per game night. The day's spend is shown in the panel.
GMW.Setup.WelcomeData: Journal texts (including those hidden from players), chat, voice transcripts and the names of characters and players are sent to the AI service. Keys and world files stay on your computer: the server listens only there and answers only your Foundry.
GMW.Setup.WelcomeTime: Setup takes about 10 minutes. Everything can be changed later in the settings (⚙ in the GM Whispers panel), and this wizard can be started again from there.
GMW.Setup.WelcomeFeedback: This is a first version for testing — feedback is welcome:
GMW.Setup.ServerHow: GM Whispers Core is the folder you unpacked during installation. Run {setup} once (it installs what's needed), then {start}. The server is started before every game — manually, by double-clicking {start}.
GMW.Setup.ServerCode: The server window shows an access code — the string the module uses to recognize its server. Paste it here.
GMW.Setup.KeyWhat: The module has no model of its own — it talks to a service where you have an account. An API key is a long string the service issues in your account; it tells the service whom to bill.
GMW.Setup.KeyWhich: One key is enough. If you're not sure what to pick: Claude and OpenAI give the best answers; OpenRouter is one key for hundreds of models, handy for trying things out. Pick a service, paste the key and press “Check” — the module picks the models itself.
GMW.Setup.CampaignIntro: This information is sent to the model with every question. Without it, the model answers in generalities based on its own idea of D&D and fantasy. The name, the system and three to five sentences about the world and tone are enough; the rest can be added later.
GMW.Setup.SourcesTitle: Step 4. What GM Whispers will use as knowledge sources
GMW.Setup.SourcesIntro: GM Whispers answers from your world's journals. So it knows what to trust when sources contradict, mark what's in each folder: your notes, the diary, the adventure text, the world description, the rules. Folders with pictures and drafts — “exclude”. If in doubt, leave “auto”.
GMW.Setup.VoiceIntro: If you play in Discord, the {craig} bot can record voice. After the game, download the recording from the bot as an archive into a folder on your computer (or set up Craig's cloud upload — a paid bot feature). Point to that folder and “Recap” will cover not just the chat but everything said at the table. Recognition runs on your GPU (NVIDIA) and costs nothing.
GMW.Setup.VoiceFormat: The best download format from Craig is multitrack FLAC (AAC/MP3 work too), one zip per session. No Discord or GPU — skip this step: recaps will use the chat and Foundry events.
GMW.Setup.CraigAuto: Transcribe new recordings as soon as they appear in the folder
GMW.Setup.DoneKb: The knowledge base will be built from the journals and the ticked rulebooks — it takes a minute or two, with progress shown in the panel. After that it updates on every journal edit.
GMW.Setup.DoneBible: The Campaign Bible — a short page about the party, NPCs and the current state of affairs that the model gets with every question — is built next and appears in the journal. You can add to the “Permanent” page yourself; we suggest reviewing and editing it every 3–4 sessions.
GMW.Setup.DoneUse1: Alt+G or the wizard hat on the token controls opens the question window. Ask anything about the world, NPCs or rules.
GMW.Setup.DoneUse2: Right-click a token → hat: “Who is this”, “Line”, “Combat turn”. Alt+T / Alt+R do the same for the selected token.
GMW.Setup.DoneUse3: Prep — a pre-session briefing to get the GM ready; Recap — after the game, builds a journal from everything that happened.
GMW.Setup.DoneSettings: All settings are under ⚙ in the panel. You can run this wizard again from there.
GMW.Setup.NeedServer: Go back to the “Server” step, run {cmd} and press “Test connection”.
GMW.Setup.LaterTooltip: Close the wizard; you can reopen it from the settings
GMW.Setup.NoServer: The server isn't responding. Run server\start.bat and check the access code.
GMW.Setup.NoKey: At least one key is needed: without it the model won't answer.
GMW.Setup.Finished: GM Whispers: setup complete. Building the knowledge base…
GMW.Changelog.Title: GM Whispers — what's new
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.1: Interface texts rewritten to be clearer, in an informal voice. The “Voice and storage” tab is now “Transcription”. New users don't see the “What's new” window — the first-run wizard opens instead.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.2: First-run wizard: opens by itself in a new world and asks for everything step by step, with explanations — server, key, campaign, sources, voice. Afterwards it only runs from the “Setup wizard” button at the bottom of ⚙.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.3: The knowledge base builds itself: on first run and after the sources change. The “KB” button is gone from the panel; “Rebuild knowledge base” stays at the bottom of the settings just in case.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.4: Simpler settings: three tabs instead of five, one API key (the service is picked from a list), rarely used fields under “Advanced”. The server address and access code now live only in the ⚙ window; the “Keep a log” and “Auto-update knowledge base” checkboxes are gone — those are always on.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.5: The panel status line is shorter: “I know N journal pages · today's spend”.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.6: The Campaign Bible moved to settings → Campaign: status, the backstories folder and the “Open” / “Build” buttons are there. The first version is built automatically along with the knowledge base. The book button is gone from the panel.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.7: The game system in the campaign profile is a list of popular systems (guessed from the Foundry world); the spoken language for transcription is a list too.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_2.8: The answer feed no longer disappears: close the panel and reopen it — everything's still there, even after F5 (the last 20 answers are kept in the browser).
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.1: “Prep” — a one-button pre-session briefing: where you left off, open threads, who's ahead, what to pull from the book, fallbacks, a checklist → the “GM Whispers · Prep” journal.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.2: Localization begins: new module texts come from lang/ru.json and lang/en.json; the “Prep” briefing answers in Foundry's language.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.3: Other game systems: on non-dnd5e systems the module works without detailed stat blocks (HP, AC, speed via generic paths); map tactics still work. Example questions are no longer tied to Drakkenheim and come in two languages; rules compendiums are suggested by name.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.4: Streaming output: the advisor's answer appears as it's generated, and while the model searches you can see what it's looking for.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.5: Answer style in ⚙ → Campaign: length (short / normal / detailed), “lines only”, “no improvisation”, “mention the player”.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.6: 📖 Campaign Bible: a two-page journal — “Permanent” (you edit it) and “Current State” (refreshed after every “Recap”); sent with every request to the model. The first version is built from backstories, the party and recaps — the book button in the panel.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.7: Campaign profile in ⚙ (name, system, world, tone, special rules, answer language) — the module is no longer tied to one campaign; your data is already filled in.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.8: Knowledge sources in ⚙: a type for each journal folder (GM materials / diary / adventure / world / rules / exclude) and compendiums as checkboxes — instead of rules based on folder names.
GMW.Changelog.0_3_0.9: New model providers: Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter and a “custom provider” with any OpenAI-compatible API (RouterAI etc.). Keys and model choice are in ⚙ “Server settings”.
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.1: ⚙ “Server settings” in the panel: API keys, models (or “auto”), the Craig folder, who's who, exclusions — no file editing.
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.2: A first-run guide in the panel until the server, key or knowledge base are ready.
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.3: Today's spend in the status line (from the server).
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.4: Hotkeys: Alt+T — tactics, Alt+R — a line for the selected token (changeable in the controls settings).
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.5: Export and import settings as a file (without keys).
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.6: Voice transcription language and retention period for old sessions — in the settings.
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.7: The server can run in the tray without a window (server\start_tray.bat).
GMW.Changelog.0_2_0.8: Security and load: editing a journal no longer rebuilds the whole knowledge base; the server answers only its own Foundry.
GMW.Changelog.0_1_0.1: Lore advisor, map tactics, session recaps into the diary, voice recording via Craig, D&D 2024 rules from compendiums.
